course_name_original: Teoría de Circuitos y Redes Eléctricas
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of electricity, as covered in the Electrical Technology course (second year of industrial engineering degrees).
Basic knowledge of physics and mathematics: differential and integral calculus, algebra and complex algebra, and electromagnetic theory.

learning_outcomes.text: Identify, analyze, and calculate balanced and unbalanced three-phase circuits, as well as select and decide on the procedures for calculating and measuring the power absorbed (or delivered) by them.
Classify and analyze electrical transients produced in first, second, and higher-order electrical circuits.
Perform current calculations when short circuits occur in electrical networks, using the symmetrical components technique.
Analyze and compare electrical networks composed of linear and non-linear elements.
Handle the analysis techniques for electrical circuits fed with non-sinusoidal periodic waves and use them for their resolution.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Electrical circuits in transient regime
Second-order and higher electrical circuits. Application of Laplace transform.
Technical characteristics of electrical energy. Justification of three-phase electrical circuits.
Three-phase electrical power. Power measurements and measuring equipment.
Topic 4. Introduction to the analysis of electrical power systems under normal operating conditions and short-circuit faults
Representation of the system in per unit.
Calculation of symmetrical and asymmetrical short circuits.
Topic 5. Non-linear circuits and non-sinusoidal supply
Harmonic distortion in electrical power systems.
Session 1. Introduction to circuit modeling in the Matlab/Simulink environment. Transient analysis of first-order circuits.
Session 2. Analysis of second-order circuits. Application of the Laplace transform.
Session 3. Harmonic distortion. Tutorial, part I.
Session 4. Harmonic distortion. Tutorial, part II.
Session 5. Analysis of short-circuit faults in electrical networks. Part I.
Session 6. Analysis of short-circuit faults in electrical networks. Part II. Application of matrix methods.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as: [Final grade] = T1*0.75 + P1*0.05 + P2*0.1 + P3*0.1. A minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required in the theory exam (T1); otherwise, the final grade will be a maximum of 4.5 points. No minimum grade is established for P1, P2, and P3. For the extraordinary call, the final grade is calculated as: [Final grade] = E1*0.75 + E2, where E2 = P1*0.05 + P2*0.1 + P3*0.1, retaining grades from the ordinary call for P1, P2, P3. A minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required in the theory exam (E1). For differentiated evaluation, the theory exam counts for 100% of the final grade, with a practical laboratory exam (EP1) as pass/fail; an 'fail' in EP1 limits the final grade to a maximum of 4.5/10 points.
